To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
high doses of LH pulses are not sufficient for formation of cystic follicles in lactating dairy heifers and cows.
high doses of LH do not necessarily cause follicular cysts in dairy cows, but do increase follicular growth and decrease time to first ovulatory cycle.

high, frequent doses (40 microg LH per hour) of exogenous luteinizing hor- mones (LHs) did not cause follicular cysts, but did stimulate follicular growth and development in both cyclic (Experiment 1) and anestrous (Experiment 2) dairy cattle.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of the hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal axis in the cow and the effects of exogenous gonadotropin administration on ovarian follicular development and oocyte competence in the cow.
understanding the mechanisms by which the ovary responds to the high levels of LH associated with follicular luteinizing cysts.
the effects of exogenous gonadotropin administration on ovarian follicular development and ovulatory function in dairy cattle.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pulsatile LH infusion at high doses does not induce cysts in dairy cows.
pulsatile infusion of LH stimulates follicular growth and follicle steroidogenesis, and decreases time to first ovulatory follicle in postpartum anestrous cows.

pulsatile administration of exogenous LH at a rate of 40 microg/h for 7 d did not cause follicular cysts in lactate dairy cows, and that pulsatile LH infusion stimulated follicular growth, steroidogenesis, and ovulatory activity in anestrous lactating dairy cows.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high concentrations of LH do not cause cyst formation in dairy cattle, but they do increase the rate of follicular growth and decrease the time to ovulation.
pulsatile infusion of LH stimulates follicular growth, increases steroidogenesis, and reduces time to ovulation in postpartum cows, but is not sufficient to induce ovulation in cows with cysts.
pulsatile administration of high concentrations of LH to cows with follicular cyst is not sufficient to induce ovulation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pulsatile administration of LH can induce ovulation in anovulatory postpartum cows.
high concentrations of LH do not cause ovarian follicular cysts in cows.

pulsatile administration of exogenous LH at doses that are associated with cyst formation in cattle can actually stimulate follicular growth and ovulation in lactating dairy heifers and postpartum cows.
